title: Hosting vendor selection for the pilot
contextText: Choosing where the Lambda pilot services will be hosted.

segments.text: Thanks for joining, Thane. For context, we need somewhere to host the services for the Lambda pick-path pilot, and we're deciding this week.
Happy to help. I'm Thane Dummyson, account manager at Estuary Cloud. I look after most of our consulting partners.
Our shortlist is Estuary's managed Kubernetes or running it ourselves on a small cluster.
I'd rather not run our own cluster for a pilot. JD's opinion, for what it's worth, is that we'd spend a week on plumbing we don't need.
That was going to be my question for you, JD. How much effort is managed Kubernetes on Estuary?
A couple of days to set up the pipelines. We've done it before on another client.
And we can give you a dedicated namespace with support included for the length of the pilot.
What about data residency? Lambda is strict about keeping floor data in the EU.
Our Frankfurt region covers that. All data stays in the EU.
Has Frankfurt been stable? I remember some noise about outages.
There were two short outages in Frankfurt last year, both under an hour. Nothing this year.
That's acceptable for a pilot.
Then I think we're agreed. We'll host the pilot on Estuary Cloud managed Kubernetes in the Frankfurt region.
Agreed.
Agreed. I'll start on the pipelines Monday.
Thane, the missing piece is pricing. What's the timeline on a committed-use quote?
I'll send you committed-use pricing by Friday February 13.
Good. Please send it to me and copy Pia.
Will do. And a small thing about me, I'm much better on email than on calls, I'm on the road a lot.
Email it is. JD, anything else you need from Thane?
Just the namespace and credentials once the contract is signed.
Those usually take a day after signature.
Then the critical path is really the pricing and our own sign-off.
Right. Let's reconvene when the pricing is in. Thanks Thane.

note.body:
# Hosting vendor selection for the pilot

**Date:** February 5
**Attendees:** Alma Mockwell (Larkspur Labs), Pia Sample (Larkspur Labs), JD (Larkspur Labs), Thane Dummyson (Estuary Cloud)

## Summary

The team chose where to host the services for the Lambda pick-path pilot. The shortlist was Estuary Cloud's managed Kubernetes versus a self-run cluster. Thane Dummyson, account manager at Estuary Cloud, joined to answer questions.

## Discussion

- JD argued against running a cluster ourselves for a pilot: a week of plumbing we don't need. Setting up pipelines on Estuary's managed Kubernetes takes a couple of days, and the team has done it before for another client.
- Estuary offers a dedicated namespace with support included for the pilot's duration.
- Lambda requires floor data to stay in the EU; Estuary's Frankfurt region covers that.
- Frankfurt had two short outages last year, both under an hour, and none this year. Pia judged that acceptable for a pilot.

## Decisions

- The pilot will be **hosted on Estuary Cloud managed Kubernetes in the Frankfurt region**.

## Action items

- **Thane Dummyson** — send committed-use pricing by Friday February 13, to Alma with Pia copied.
- **JD** — start on the deployment pipelines on Monday.
- Namespace and credentials follow about a day after contract signature.

## Notes

- Thane is much easier to reach by email than on calls; he travels a lot.
- The critical path is now the pricing and Larkspur's own sign-off.
